title: FizzBuzz
statement: Write a function `fizzBuzz(n)` that returns an array of the numbers from 1 to `n` as strings, except: multiples of 3 become `'Fizz'`, multiples of 5 become `'Buzz'`, and multiples of both become `'FizzBuzz'`. For example, `fizzBuzz(5)` returns `['1', '2', 'Fizz', '4', 'Buzz']`.
fallbackHints: You will make one answer for each number from 1 up to n. What shape of code repeats a step for a range of numbers?
The remainder operator tells you whether one number divides evenly into another. The order in which you check the rules matters, so think about which rule is the most specific.
If you check 'divisible by 3' first, a number like 15 gets the wrong word. Check the case that needs both conditions before the single-condition cases. Also remember every entry must be a string.
